claim: Martian Code Review Bench (2026) evaluated 17 AI code review tools across 200,000+ real pull requests, defining precision as the share of review comments that lead to an actual code change and recall as the share of real issues caught; top tools clustered around ~50% precision and ~50% recall.
quote: Precision: the percentage of a tool's review comments that lead to an actual code change... Recall: the percentage of real issues in a PR that the tool actually catches... F1 Score: 51.7%, Precision: 52.2%, Recall: 51.1%

claim: A two-phase field study at WirelessCar (7 interview + 10 experiment participants) found developers warn that noisy or low-priority AI review comments cause reviewers to stop reading and miss real issues, a key trust failure mode.
quote: The problem with those kinds of checks is that, if they're not good enough, you stop reading them... you miss the real issues because you start ignoring the feedback

claim: Evaluating GPT-4o and Gemini 2.0 Flash on 492 AI-generated code blocks, correctness accuracy was only 68.5% (GPT-4o) / 63.9% (Gemini) and dropped up to 22.87% without problem descriptions, leading authors to conclude LLMs are unreliable for fully automated review and recommend human-in-the-loop.
quote: LLMs would be unreliable in a fully automated code review environment... Correctness Accuracy 68.50% (GPT-4o) 63.89% (Gemini)... differences up to 22.87% observed in correction and regression ratios

claim: In an industrial study at Tencent, the static analysis tool's baseline false-positive rate was ~76% (>90% before filtering), and the best LLM method (LLM4PFA) eliminated 94-98% of false positives at 0.93-0.94 accuracy on 433 alarms.
quote: LLM4PFA...eliminates 94-98% of false positives across different backbone LLMs... false positive rate 76% in the final dataset, with the actual rate higher than 90%... 433 total alarms (328 false positives, 105 true positives)

claim: A study of 6 LLMs across 17 CVEs in 10 real-world projects found that 'bug-free' framing systematically degrades vulnerability detection (confirmation bias), and an iterative refinement attack exploiting this bias achieves a 100% success rate.
quote: 6 LLMs under five framing conditions... 17 CVEs across 10 real-world projects... iterative refinement attack...achieves 100% success... bug-free framing producing the strongest effect

claim: A case study of 16 GitHub Actions AI reviewers across 178 mature repos (22,326 AI comments) found only 0.9-19.2% of valid AI comments led to code changes versus ~60% for human comments, with hunk-level and manually-triggered tools (12.8% vs 6.8%) faring better.
quote: 0.9%-19.2% for valid AI-generated comments depending on the tool... 60% of valid human review comments led to code changes... 12.8% addressing rate for manually triggered comments versus 6.8% for automatically triggered ones

claim: Analyzing 278,790 review conversations across 300 OSS projects, AI agent comments were ~7x more verbose than humans (29.6 vs 4.1 tokens/line), concentrated >95% on code-improvement/defect-detection, and had a 16.6% adoption rate versus 56.5% for humans.
quote: 29.6 tokens per line of code... 4.1 tokens per line of code... Code Improvement and Defect Detection include over 95% of AI agent comments... Human reviewers: 56.5%... AI agents: 16.6%

claim: Hallucinations in LLM code review include fabricated package recommendations ('slopsquatting': 19.7% of 576,000 sampled packages were non-existent, 58% repeated across queries), enabling supply-chain attacks; standard AI code review carries reported 5-15% false-positive rates.
quote: 19.7% of recommended packages (205,000 total) were fabricated and non-existent... 58% of hallucinated packages repeated across multiple queries... standard AI code review generating 5-15% false positive rates
